tools.name: fetch-transcript
tools.title: Fetch Transcript
tools.description: Fetches the transcript of a YouTube video as plain text so it can be summarised, translated, or turned into notes.
tools.instructions: Use this whenever the user references a YouTube video and needs its spoken content - for summarising, translating, extracting quotes, or writing notes. Requires the yt-dlp command-line tool to be installed on the user's machine; if the tool reports it is missing, tell the user to install it with 'brew install yt-dlp'. The transcript is auto-generated by YouTube, so expect missing punctuation and occasional mis-transcribed words. Long videos can be very large: pass maxLength to cap the response. If truncated is true you are not holding the complete transcript, either because earlier text was skipped or because later text was cut off. When nextOffset is not null, call the tool again with offset set to that value to read the following chunk. Never describe a video as fully covered while truncated is true; say instead which part your answer is based on.

ai.instructions: This extension reads the transcript of a YouTube video. It only reads: it never uploads, edits, or deletes anything on YouTube. When the user asks what a video says, always fetch the transcript rather than guessing from the URL or the title. If a transcript comes back truncated, say so plainly instead of presenting a partial summary as complete.

fetch-transcript.title: Example Video
fetch-transcript.transcript: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are looking at three ways to speed up your morning routine.
